title: Computational Phenomenology of Borderline Personality Disorder: A Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Simulated Expert Personas and Human Clinical Experts
abstract: arXiv:2508.19008v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Building on a human-led thematic analysis of clinical life-story interviews (> 150,000 words) with inpatients with Borderline Personality Disorder, this study examines the capacity of large language models (OpenAI's GPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude) to support qualitative clinical analysis. The models' interpretative potential was evaluated using a mixed-methods approach. Study A involved blinded and non-blinded judges in phenomenology and clinical psychology. The experts assessed the validity of AI-generated content using semantic congruence, Jaccard coefficients, and multidimensional validity ratings, including credibility, coherence, the substantiveness of results, and grounding in qualitative data. translated_title: 边缘型人格障碍的计算现象学：LLM模拟专家角色与人类临床专家的比较评估
translated_abstract: 基于一项由人类主导的对边缘型人格障碍住院患者临床生活史访谈（超过15万字）的主题分析，本研究考察了大型语言模型（OpenAI的GPT、Google的Gemini和Anthropic的Claude）支持定性临床分析的能力。通过混合方法评估了模型的解释潜力。研究A涉及现象学和临床心理学领域的盲审与非盲审评判者，专家们使用语义一致性、Jaccard系数和多维有效性评级（包括可信度、连贯性、结果的实质性及定性数据基础）评估了AI生成内容的有效性。在研究B中，使用神经方法将人类和模型生成的主题描述嵌入多维向量空间，该方法提供了人类与模型之间差异的客观化计算度量。
tldr: 本研究通过混合方法比较评估了LLM模拟专家与人类临床专家在边缘型人格障碍定性分析中的表现，发现LLM在支持临床主题分析方面具有潜力但存在差异。
en_tdlr: This study comparatively evaluates LLM-simulated expert personas versus human clinical experts in qualitative analysis of Borderline Personality Disorder, revealing LLMs' potential and differences in supporting clinical thematic analysis.
